jobs.title: Senior Environmental Data Manager
jobs.description:
Overview

Do you want to build an impactful career to change the world for the better?

Geosyntec has an exciting opportunity for a Senior Environmental Data Manager
to join our team in Oakland, Walnut Creek, Davis, or Sacramento, California
. In this role, you will support the development and management of environmental data systems, workflows, and quality processes for multidisciplinary projects involving environmental assessment, groundwater remediation, water resources, geotechnical construction, and related services. You will combine environmental chemistry expertise with strong database, automation, and client-service skills to deliver accurate, accessible, and decision-ready information.

Geosyntec is an innovative, international engineering and consulting firm serving private and public-sector clients to address new ventures and complex problems involving our environment, natural resources, and civil infrastructure. Our engineers, scientists, technical and project employees serve our clients from offices across the world. Ranked by ENR as one of the top environmental engineering design firms, Geosyntec is internationally known for its technical leadership, broad experience, and exceptional client service.

We invest in our people. Each employee is unique, and your career at Geosyntec will be too. We offer competitive pay and benefits, and well-being programs to support you and your family.

To Learn More Visit: http://www.geosyntec.com/careers/ .

Essential Duties And Responsibilities

Design, develop, and manage project-specific relational database applications using enterprise platforms such as Microsoft SQL Server and EQuIS.
Create documented workflows and metadata that automate the integration of data from multiple sources and deliver it to maps, reports, dashboards, and other tools.
Manage environmental datasets across the full data lifecycle, from planning and collection through analysis and final reporting.
Establish and perform QA/QC for environmental data, systems, and related processes.
Compile, verify, analyze, and report large, complex, and diverse datasets.
Coordinate with laboratories, consultants, agencies, and other internal and external data providers to support accurate, timely data collection and transfer.
Collect, transform, query, and analyze environmental analytical, geologic, geotechnical, and geospatial data.
Interact with internal and external clients to deliver database management and data-visualization solutions for environmental, engineering, and geoscience projects.
Drive personal , company, and rental vehicles to client or company project or office sites, and other business locations, as needed.

You will collaborate with experienced professionals across disciplines while contributing your own technical expertise and perspective. Geosyntec supports continuous learning, encourages employees to deepen their interests and skills, and recognizes advancement through performance, initiative, and impact.

Education and Licensure

Bachelor's degree in environmental science, chemistry, geography, computer science, engineering, or geology. (required)
Advanced degree in environmental science, chemistry, geography, computer science, engineering, or geology. (preferred)

Skills, Experience And Qualifications

At lea st 8 years of technical training and experience in relational database technology, or equivalent combination of education and experience. (required)
Demonstrated experience managing databases and developing ETL processes. ( required)
Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel and Access, including complex formulas and effective data visualization. (required)
Ability to write complex SQL queries and automate routine processes. (required)
Experience automating processes with scripting languages such as Python or R. (required)
Strong analytical, troubleshooting, and problem-solving capabilities. (required)
Exceptional attention to detail across quantitative work products and written communications. (required)
Proficiency with EarthSoft’s EQuIS environmental data management platform. (preferred)
Direct experience managing environmental, geologic, and geotechnical data collection. (preferred)
Knowledge of laboratory analytical data verification and validation processes. (preferred)
Experience submitting data to and retrieving data from agency and government databases, including California Water Boards GeoTracker, CIWQS, NIRIS, ERPIMS, and CEDEN. (preferred)
Valid U.S. driver’s license and a satisfactory driving record for business travel. (required)

This opportunity will be posted for at least five days. Below are the potential compensation ranges that we in good faith believe are applicable for this role at the time of this posting and are only applicable for jobs to be performed in the specified location(s) below. The typical base salary range for this position is just one component of Geosyntec’s total compensation package for employees. Actual compensation will be determined based on education, experience, skill set and location.

Minimum Salary: $127,530 /year / Maximum Salary: $178,540 /year (Oakland, CA, Walnut Creek, CA)
Minimum Salary: $121,985 /year / Maximum Salary: $170,780 /year (Davis, CA, Sacramento, CA)

We offer a comprehensive benefits package including, paid holidays, vacation, sick, and personal paid time off, medical, dental, vision, life, and disability insurance, 401(k), and other benefits to eligible employees.

jobs.title: Environmental Scientist/Geologist
jobs.description:
Arcadis is the world's leading company delivering sustainable design, engineering, and consultancy solutions for natural and built assets.

We are more than 34,000 people, in over 30 countries, dedicated to improving quality of life. Everyone has an important role to play. With the power of many curious minds, together we can solve the world’s most complex challenges and deliver more impact together.

Role description:

Arcadis is seeking an entry-level
Geologist/Environmental Scientist to join our team in San Francisco, CA or Concord, CA. While this position requires both field and office work, the candidate should expect to spend 50% to 75% of their time in the field.

You will have the opportunity to join a dedicated team in San Francisco, CA or Concord, CA that prioritizes mentorship and your professional growth. The team is committed to supporting your success and providing guidance as you navigate your role.

We are currently considering candidates available for an immediate start and those seeking a Summer 2027 start date.

As part of our Resilience Environment team, you’ll help improve quality of life.

Role accountabilities:

As part of this role, you will be responsible for assisting Project Managers (PMs) and Task Managers (TMs) in planning and executing environmental site characterization, investigation, and remediation tasks.

Fieldwork will also be a key aspect of this position, which will offer you an opportunity to be trained to oversee drilling for soil sampling and groundwater well installation, groundwater sampling, subcontractor oversight, operation and maintenance of remediation systems, vapor intrusion/soil gas surveys, among other tasks. It is essential to conduct fieldwork with a focus on health and safety.

Your core duties will include:

Prepare subcontracts and oversee the work of subcontractors.
Writing and preparing technical reports, work plans, letters, and memoranda
Office work may include task coordination, data compilation and interpretation, cost estimates, health & safety plan preparation, report writing, regulatory file reviews, proposal writing, project strategy development, schedule and budget management, and establishment of subcontracts.
Conduct field work including soil, groundwater, and/or vapor sampling in the field. Field work will require regional business travel for up to 1-2 days per week on average. A few times per year, travel will be required within the U.S. for up to two weeks at a time.

To be successful in this role, you should possess strong written and oral communication skills, be self-motivated, and exhibit independent thinking. You should be able to work effectively and efficiently in a team setting as well as independently and remotely. Successful candidates will demonstrate their ability to be adaptable, creative problem solvers who can work collaboratively as a team member.

In summary, this position encompasses both office work (task management, data analysis, report preparation, scope preparation, and client communications) as well as field work. Fieldwork will also be a key aspect of this position, which will offer you an opportunity to be trained to oversee drilling for soil sampling and groundwater well installation, groundwater sampling, subcontractor oversight, operation and maintenance of remediation systems, vapor intrusion/soil gas surveys, among other tasks. Additionally, Arcadis supports many of our client’s needs when unforeseen incidents occur, such as train derailments, pipeline releases, etc. An aspect of this role is supporting our National emergency response teams to ensure rapid protection of human health and the environment. This work is completed under the direction of trained incident responders and may require unanticipated travel and work outside standard business hours.

Field work will require regional business travel for up to 1-2 days per week on average. A few times per year, travel will be required within the U.S. for up to two weeks at a time. Estimated travel is up to 75% during the first two years, with travel reduced with career growth. By the third year, travel for field work is typically 50%. Travel expenses are reimbursable. A valid driver's license is required for the role.

Qualifications & Experience:

Required Qualifications

Bachelor’s of Science in Geology, Hydrogeology, or closely related field (i.e., environmental science, physical science)

Preferred Qualifications

Master of Science degree in Geology or closely related field
Current OSHA 40-hour HAZWOPER training 

Why Arcadis?

We can only achieve our goals when everyone is empowered to be their best. We believe everyone's contribution matters. It’s why we are pioneering a skills-based approach, where you can harness your unique experience and expertise to carve your career path and maximize the impact we can make together.

You’ll do meaningful work, and no matter what role, you’ll be helping to deliver sustainable solutions for a more prosperous planet. Make your mark, on your career, your colleagues, your clients, your life and the world around you.

Together, we can create a lasting legacy.

Join Arcadis. Create a Legacy.

Our Commitment to Equality, Diversity, Inclusion & Belonging

We want you to be able to bring your best self to work every day. Our ambition is to be an employer of choice and provide a great place to work for all our people. We are an equal opportunity employer. We are dedicated to a policy of non-discrimination in employment on any basis including race, creed, color, religion, national origin, sex, age, disability, marital status, sexual orientation, gender identity, citizenship status, disability, veteran status, or any other basis prohibited by law.

Arcadis offers benefits for full time and part time positions. These benefits include medical, dental, and vision, EAP, 401K, STD, LTD, AD&D, life insurance, paid parental leave, reward & recognition program and optional benefits including wellbeing benefits, adoption assistance and tuition reimbursement. We offer nine paid holidays and 15 days PTO that accrue per year. The salary range for this position is $63,480- $95,220. Actual salaries will vary and are based on several factors, such as experience, education, budget, internal equity, project and location.

jobs.title: Senior Agrochemical Regulatory Affairs Consultant
jobs.description:
Job Description

Inviting bright minds

Do you want to push the boundaries of your profession and develop your excellence in an open, collaborative and empowering culture? We work to create a sustainable future and our inspiring projects and innovative solutions aim to set the standard among our peers. You will join a global company that has been growing successfully since its founding in 1945. Together, we lead and leave a positive impact on societies, companies and people around the world. Ramboll Health Science Spearhead has approx. 360 bright minds globally and you can become one of them in our Australia team contributing to our continued success.

You will join our Environment and Health Business Unit

As our new Senior Consultant, you will have experience and be a subject matter expert in Agrochemical regulations in Australia (APVMA) and New Zealand (EPA and ACVM). You will bring the ability to organize, coordinate and communicate across an interdisciplinary team, engaging externally with technical professionals, and regulatory agencies. You will provide strategic expertise and support the preparation of regulatory submissions for a variety of agrochemical related products in the region. A strong customer service ethic and ability to multitask is vital for this role. You will present a positive “can-do” attitude and be a self-starter within a team of dedicated professionals.

This is a unique opportunity to have a role within the Ramboll Health Science Spearhead to help drive the growth of the agrochemical consulting business in Australia, working with our international team of regulatory and technical experts, while advancing your skills and consulting career. Reporting to the Principal, Health Sciences in Australia your role would be based at one of Ramboll’s Australian Offices.

Your key tasks and responsibility will be:

Support the execution of Product Stewardship and Safety projects with a focus on Australian and New Zealand plant protection registrations
Act as project manager for interdisciplinary agrochemical regulatory projects
Responsible for strategic guidance and translating complex scientific information into regulator-ready submissions.
Advise clients on existing as well as upcoming regulatory obligations (in the fields of environmental, health & safety-related topics)
Developing strategies, market analysis and helping to expand and drive the growth of Ramboll’s agrochemical business in the region.
Active in business development, meeting clients and attending appropriate conferences and seminars to increase Ramboll’s visibility in the region.

Your starting point for constant growth

From the moment you join Ramboll, we will support your personal and professional developments so that you grow with the company. For this role, we believe your starting point is:

Ability to provide strategic advice and determine practical compliance solutions to meet our clients’ commercial aims for their agricultural related products.
Experience leading multi-faceted teams on projects, producing a high-quality work product, on time and within budget
Ability to guide clients through registrations, variations, and label/claims strategies, helping to prepare compliance advice, application dossiers and data-gap analyses.
Staying current with changes in regulatory landscape affecting Ramboll’s clients and maintaining contacts and relationships with regulatory authorities.
Proficiency assessing the impact of new regional regulations on the business and participates in actions to assist our clients in dealing with the implementation of these new regulations.
Strong team player and customer-oriented approach.

Qualifications

Desired skills/experience

A minimum of 7 years’ industry or consulting experience with plant protection product registration in Australia and New Zealand
Scientific background preferably with a degree or higher in agriculture, veterinary medicine, chemistry, biology or a related discipline
Ability to handle multiple tasks and work streams in a fast-paced environment while maintaining outstanding attention to detail and quality of deliverables
Experience/comfort with working in a virtual team with stakeholders across geographies
Ability to support internal and external clients with both technical and strategic consulting services
Experience in business development would be advantageous
Strong written and oral communication skills
Good presentation skills and business sense
Demonstrated problem-solving skills
Possess a drive and personal initiative to keep learning and improving in the chosen field.

Additional Information

Welcome to our Environment & Health division

Ramboll develops innovative, scientifically sound solutions that help increase livability by reducing pollution and restoring natural environments. One of the world’s leading environmental and health consultancies, our bright minds are trusted by clients to manage their most challenging environmental, health and social issues.

Ramboll in Asia Pacific

Ramboll has close to 500 experts working across more than 10 offices in Asia Pacific. We are present in Australia, China, Hong Kong SAR, Malaysia, India, Japan, South Korea and Singapore. Our experts are applying their passion to deliver innovative and sustainable solutions in markets as diverse as Buildings, Transport, Water, Environment & Health, Energy and Architecture &, Landscape. Founded in Denmark, Ramboll is a people company. We invite you to contribute to a sustainable future working in an open, collaborative and empowering culture.

Work at the heart of sustainable change with Ramboll in Asia Pacific

Ramboll is a global architecture, engineering, and consultancy company. As a foundation-owned people company, founded in Denmark, we believe that the purpose of sustainable change is to create a thriving world for both nature and people. So, that’s where we start – and how we work. Our history is rooted in a clear vision of how a responsible company should act and being open and curious is a cornerstone of our culture. Ramboll in Asia Pacific has close to 500 people working across ten offices. Ramboll experts deliver innovative solutions across Buildings, Transport, Water, Environment & Health, Energy, and Architecture & Landscape.

Equality, Diversity, and Inclusion

Equality, diversity, and inclusion are at the heart of what we do. At Ramboll, we believe that diversity is a strength and that different experiences and perspectives are essential to creating truly sustainable societies. We are committed to providing an inclusive and supportive work environment where everyone is able to flourish and reach their potential. We also know how important it is to achieve the right balance of where, when, and how much you work. At Ramboll, we offer flexibility as part of our positive and inclusive approach to work. We invite applications from candidates of all backgrounds and characteristics.

Ready to join us?

Please submit your application with your up-to-date CV. We invite diversity in all its forms and encourage applicants from all groups to apply.

Thank you for taking the time to apply! We look forward to receiving your application.
